question: Frontex is now using space surveillance to detect high-frequency radio signals in order to identify, for example, ships that cannot be located. Tracking the locations of satellite phones could help the agency find boats carrying refugees. 1.

Under which contracts (e.g. the MAS service in the Mediterranean) does Frontex also have access to data from radio-frequency transmitter detectors to trace signals from mobile or satellite phones or other radio signals, and which companies benefit from this?
What contracts did Frontex conclude with Kleos, Unseenlabs, HawkEye360 or Horizon Technologies in 2022, 2023 and 2024, and what is the specific scope of these contracts?
To what extent do satellites or aircraft commissioned by Frontex also have detectors to trace radar emissions, and who are the manufacturers?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (19.6.2024) As the question regarding ‘Frontex’s use of spying equipment’ falls entirely under the responsibility of the European Border and Coast Guard Agency (Frontex), the Commission has asked the Agency to provide the details requested by the Honourable Member. The Agency’s reply will be sent by the Commission to the Honourable Member as soon as possible.
